title: Self-Funded Health, PBM & Workers' Comp Arbitrage

economics.owner_net_profit_potential: $38,400–$551,000 USD annually, before personal taxes and reinvestment
economics.includes_contractors_note: Headcount includes the working owner and recurring contractors as people, not FTE equivalents. Contractors may be part-time. Scaled scenario adds one employee and one contractor; external vendor workforces are not counted as internal team members.
economics.revenue_basis: Net retained PEPM benefits advisory fees, stop-loss/TPA commissions, and contingent Workers' Comp E-Mod refund splits; excludes employer claim funds and insurance premiums
economics.cost_basis: Annual net margins include operating expenses and non-owner labor; monthly opex is fixed/semi-fixed overhead only. No owner salary is deducted. Capital needs may grow beyond startup range.
economics.estimate_status: Illustrative assumptions; not verified earnings data

regulatory_notes: Hold active state Life & Health and Property & Casualty producer licenses and deliver full ERISA §408(b)(2) / CAA 2021 compensation disclosures.
Structure stop-loss specific/aggregate attachment points, run-out coverage, and RBP balance-bill legal defense cleanly.

inputs: Public Form 5500 filings and available Schedule A/C records, employer size and plan-year information, employer-confirmed renewal dates and appropriately obtained business contact details.

Employer authorization, incumbent fee disclosures, plan documents, aggregate claims and pharmacy reports, stop-loss terms, underwriting requirements and privacy-controlled access to necessary participant information.

Licensed broker and specialist relationships, TPA and stop-loss proposals, captive participation terms, PBM rebate and spread definitions, NADAC availability and fallback pricing rules, and a $40–$65 PEPM service proposal.
plays.mechanism: Use public Form 5500 Schedule A/C information, where filed and informative, to identify mid-market renewal and compensation-review opportunities, then offer an employer-authorized CAA 2021 service-provider fee-disclosure review. A properly licensed advisory team can seek broker-of-record appointments and compare bundled coverage with separately contracted TPA, stop-loss or suitable captive arrangements and a transparent pass-through PBM using an explicitly defined NADAC-based pricing methodology. Negotiate recurring $40–$65 PEPM advisory fees where supported by scope and client agreement, with all commissions and indirect compensation disclosed and no assumption that unbundling guarantees savings.
metrics: Recurring advisory revenue: enrolled employees multiplied by the contracted $40–$65 PEPM fee, less servicing costs and disclosed fee offsets.
Risk-adjusted employer cost: claims, administration, stop-loss premiums, pharmacy costs, collateral and runout obligations minus realized rebates and recoveries.
Service and retention quality: renewal retention, disclosure completeness, pharmacy guarantee reconciliation variance and unresolved participant access issues.
plays.name: Mid-Market Level-Funded Benefits and Transparent PBM Advisory Operator

platform_risks.detection_metric: Adverse-scenario funding gap, claims-to-budget variance, unrecovered stop-loss balances and unexplained differences between disclosed and received compensation.
platform_risks.failure_mode: The proposed unbundled plan produces adverse claims exposure or undisclosed compensation despite appearing cheaper on headline premiums.
platform_risks.fallback: Retain or competitively rebid the existing structure when risk-adjusted economics are unfavorable, obtain explicit pricing fallbacks and narrow the engagement to disclosed advisory work until implementation conditions are satisfied.
platform_risks.impact: Employer costs exceed projections, coverage continuity deteriorates and advisory fees or the BOR relationship become disputed.
platform_risks.trigger: Incomplete claims data, stop-loss lasers or exclusions, nonrefundable captive collateral, ambiguous PBM rebate definitions or unsupported NADAC pricing for uncovered products.

workflow: 1. Analyze publicly available filings through permitted access methods, identify likely renewal opportunities and confirm current plan arrangements directly because filings are historical and may omit relevant compensation details.
2. Obtain employer authorization, review applicable CAA 2021 disclosures and existing termination terms, and define advisory deliverables and compensation before requesting any BOR appointment.

3. Compare fully insured and level-funded options using expected and adverse claims scenarios, stop-loss exclusions and lasers, captive collateral, TPA fees, pharmacy guarantees and rebates actually retained by the employer.

4. Implement the employer-selected structure with licensed parties, privacy safeguards and continuity planning; collect agreed PEPM fees and review total costs, disclosures and service performance at each renewal.

inputs: Customer authorization, three to four years of policies and premium audits, payroll registers, job-duty evidence, overtime breakdowns, officer election documents and subcontractor coverage records.
Applicable state classification rules, NCCI or independent-bureau worksheets, experience-period and valuation dates, carrier loss runs and documented claim corrections.
Carrier and bureau dispute procedures, policy-specific correction deadlines, a 30%–40% realized-refund agreement and licensed brokerage support for any BOR renewal engagement.
plays.mechanism: Audit three to four historical policy years where carrier, state and rating-bureau correction rules permit, checking actual duties, payroll classifications, eligible overtime adjustments and officer exclusions or limits. Reconcile NCCI experience-rating worksheets, or the applicable independent bureau's equivalent, to accurate carrier loss reports and valuation dates; an open reserve is not an error merely because the ultimate claim later costs less. Recover documented premium overpayments for a negotiated 30%–40% contingency and pursue separately authorized, properly licensed BOR renewal work.
metrics: Realized premium recovery: received refunds and usable policy credits divided by audited historical premium, segmented by payroll, classification and experience-mod correction.
Correction conversion: dollars recovered divided by dollars submitted, alongside days from supported dispute to revised audit or bureau worksheet.
Renewal economics: separately disclosed brokerage revenue and verified prospective premium effect, controlling for payroll, operations, rates and coverage changes.
plays.name: Workers' Compensation Classification and Experience-Mod Recovery Operator

platform_risks.detection_metric: Rejected correction dollars by reason, percentage of payroll supported by contemporaneous records and net premium change after the full audit.
platform_risks.failure_mode: A carrier or rating bureau rejects proposed corrections because classifications, loss valuations or retroactive deadlines were misinterpreted.
platform_risks.fallback: Withdraw unsupported claims, disclose any additional premium exposure, use the bureau's documented dispute process for defensible items and improve prospective payroll and claims reporting.
platform_risks.impact: No refund is issued, advisory effort is unrecovered and a broader audit may identify additional premium owed.
platform_risks.trigger: Unsupported separation of payroll, missing officer elections, treatment of later reserve reductions as historical errors or submission outside the permitted correction period.

workflow: 1. Map each policy to its governing state and bureau rules, establish the allowable correction window and reconcile audited payroll to contemporaneous employment and job-duty records.
2. Test class-code assignments, permitted overtime premium exclusions, officer elections or payroll limits and subcontractor treatment without relabeling work merely to obtain a cheaper rate.
3. Reconcile experience-mod inputs against losses reported for the applicable valuation date; submit evidenced payroll, classification or loss-data corrections to the carrier and bureau as required.
4. Obtain revised audits or rating worksheets, trace resulting premium credits through endorsements and receipts, collect the 30%–40% contingency and separately quote licensed BOR renewal services.

plays.name: Employer Self-Funded ERISA Plan International Specialty-Drug Importation Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Contracting with mid-market US employers (100–5,000 employees) operating self-funded ERISA health plans to carve out high-cost specialty biologics and GLP-1s ($6,000–$15,000/mo US PBM list price) and source the identical manufacturer-sealed drugs from licensed Tier-1 pharmacies in Canada, the UK, Australia, and New Zealand at $800–$2,200/mo—waiving the employee's copay to $0 while taking 25–35% of the employer's $50,000–$100,000/yr per-patient savings.
inputs: Department of Labor (DOL) Form 5500 Schedule A/C database identifying self-funded ERISA employers by broker, TPA, and stop-loss carrier
Licensed international pharmacy dispensation network across Tier-1 jurisdictions (Canada, UK, Australia, New Zealand) with cold-chain courier logistics
Turnkey ERISA Summary Plan Description (SPD) 'Specialty Drug Carve-Out Amendment' and $0-copay patient concierge portal
workflow: Mine DOL Form 5500 filings to target CFOs and benefits directors of self-funded companies with 150–3,000 covered lives
Audit the employer's anonymized pharmacy claims file to flag the 1–3% of members driving 45–60% of total drug spend (Humira, Stelara, Skyrizi, Dupixent, Enbrel, Ozempic)
Plug in a voluntary $0-copay international personal-importation program alongside the existing TPA, fulfilling 90-day cold-chain prescriptions at 60–80% below US PBM prices
Bill the self-funded employer plan a shared-savings contingency fee equal to 25–35% of verified net claim reduction ($15,000–$30,000/yr per enrolled specialty patient)
metrics: Verified annual specialty-claim savings ($) per self-funded employer group
Net shared-savings fee revenue ($15k–$30k/yr) per enrolled specialty patient
Employee $0-copay opt-in conversion rate (target: >85%)

platform_risks.failure_mode: Incumbent PBM rebate-contract retaliation or cold-chain customs shipment delay
platform_risks.trigger: Legacy PBM threatening to withhold formulary rebates if specialty scripts are carved out, or border clearance delays on temperature-sensitive biologics
platform_risks.impact: Delayed employer onboarding or need for local emergency bridge fills
platform_risks.detection_metric: Cold-chain transit temperature telemetry and net employer savings after accounting for any forfeited PBM rebates
platform_risks.fallback: Target independent TPAs and transparent pass-through PBMs first, combine international sourcing with US Manufacturer Patient Assistance Program (PAP) optimization, and maintain domestic bridge-fill coverage

plays.name: 340B Contract-Pharmacy & Covered-Entity Drug Price Spread Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Partnering with HRSA-qualified 340B Covered Entities (Federally Qualified Health Centers, Ryan White clinics, disproportionate-share rural hospitals) to provide turnkey Third-Party Administrator (TPA) split-billing software, specialty contract-pharmacy fulfillment, and tele-referral capture—buying outpatient specialty medications at 25–50%+ statutory 340B discounts while collecting 100% full commercial insurance reimbursement and splitting the multi-thousand-dollar per-script margin via compliant flat administrative/dispensing fees.
inputs: HRSA OPAIS (Office of Pharmacy Affairs Information System) database of Covered Entities and registered contract pharmacies
340B split-billing / virtual-inventory accumulator software tracking 11-digit NDCs, prescriber NPIs, and patient-eligibility encounters
Licensed specialty/mail-order contract pharmacy network and commercial payer PBMs
workflow: Identify under-monetized 340B Covered Entities (FQHCs, grantees, rural hospitals) with low specialty capture rates in the HRSA OPAIS registry
Deploy split-billing TPA software and mail-order specialty contract-pharmacy infrastructure that captures commercially insured prescriptions written or co-managed by clinic providers
Reimburse the pharmacy at full commercial payer rates ($3,000–$12,000/script) while replenishing drug inventory via the clinic's 340B wholesaler account at $800–$4,000/script
Charge fixed fair-market-value per-dispense administrative, software, and clinical-management fees that capture a major share of the net spread while funding the clinic's safety-net mission
metrics: Captured commercially insured 340B scripts per month per Covered Entity
Gross commercial-to-340B acquisition spread ($1,500–$6,000+) per specialty fill
HRSA audit pass rate (zero duplicate Medicaid discount or diversion findings)

platform_risks.failure_mode: Manufacturer contract-pharmacy restriction policies or HRSA 'patient definition' audit findings
platform_risks.trigger: Drug manufacturers restricting 340B replenishment to a single contract pharmacy unless claims data is submitted, or filling scripts for patients without a documented clinic encounter
platform_risks.impact: Loss of 340B ceiling price on specific NDCs or HRSA repayment liability
platform_risks.detection_metric: 100% EHR encounter-to-NPI match verification prior to 340B replenishment accumulation and automated ESP (340B ESP) data submission
platform_risks.fallback: Operate an in-house entity-owned specialty pharmacy location alongside contract pharmacies, automate 340B ESP claims-data uploads to unlock restricted NDCs, and enforce strict EHR encounter gates

plays.name: Automated Form 8850 WOTC (Work Opportunity Tax Credit) & Section 41 R&D Contingency Engine
plays.mechanism: Automate employer-authorized WOTC screening and separately substantiate Section 41 research credits, earning outcome-linked service fees only where permitted; program authorization, qualifying activities, wage coordination, and professional fee restrictions govern each claim.
inputs: Consented hiring records, Form 8850 responses, and payroll hours
Research project evidence and qualified expense ledgers
State workforce certification procedures and tax-year credit and fee rules
workflow: 1. Confirm WOTC authorization for each hire date and complete required prescreening by the job-offer date
2. Submit Form 8850 and required supporting forms within the applicable 28-day deadline and track state certification and qualifying hours
3. Separately document Section 41 qualifying research and expenses, reconciling wage overlap and applicable deduction adjustments with a tax professional
4. Obtain employer and preparer approval before filing, retain audit support, and collect permitted fees without guaranteeing credits
metrics: Timely WOTC certification submission rate
Substantiated credits realized by the employer
Net permitted service fees after review and filing costs

platform_risks.failure_mode: Credit denial or impermissible contingent-fee arrangement
platform_risks.trigger: Expired program authority, late certification, unsupported research expenses, or restricted practitioner compensation
platform_risks.impact: Reduced credits, amended returns, penalties, and fee repayment exposure
platform_risks.detection_metric: Deadline exceptions, certification denials, and unsupported expense share
platform_risks.fallback: Exclude unsupported claims and use compliant fixed-fee payroll and research-documentation services under independent tax review

plays.name: SEC Form 8-K, Form D & C-Suite Turnover Trigger Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Parse SEC EDGAR real-time RSS/JSON feeds for Form D (private Reg D capital raises) and Form 8-K (Item 5.02 C-suite departures, Item 1.01 material agreements, Item 2.01 M&A closings) to trigger sub-hour executive outreach before commercial databases update.
inputs: SEC EDGAR real-time Submissions API & Form D / Form 8-K XML feeds
Automated filing parser extracting raise amounts, executive names, & signatory contacts
Enterprise recruiting, specialty finance, & B2B agency deal-routing desk
workflow: Ingest SEC EDGAR filings within seconds of publication using a compliant User-Agent header (<=10 requests/second)
Extract Form D issuers raising $2M–$50M (who immediately deploy capital on hiring, growth agencies, and software) and Form 8-K executive transitions
Deliver tailored briefings to the filing officers and route warm introductions to executive search firms, enterprise software resellers, and B2B agencies
metrics: EDGAR publication-to-enrichment latency (seconds)
Form D / 8-K executive response rate vs. cold baseline (3–5x lift)
Retainer and placement referral fees generated per 100 filings

platform_risks.failure_mode: SEC EDGAR automated-access block or Reg D general-solicitation confusion
platform_risks.trigger: Exceeding SEC EDGAR's 10-requests-per-second fair-access limit or omitting the mandatory contact User-Agent header
platform_risks.impact: Temporary IP block by Akamai/SEC infrastructure
platform_risks.detection_metric: Request rate strictly <=5 req/sec with compliant User-Agent and zero HTTP 403 responses
platform_risks.fallback: Enforce token-bucket rate limiting at 5 req/sec and mirror SEC nightly bulk zip archives for historical lookbacks

plays.name: Public-Record & API Intelligence
plays.mechanism: Ingest fragmented county dockets, probate registries, unclaimed property ledgers, and public APIs to surface uncontested claims or high-intent B2B triggers before manual competitors.
inputs: Court & probate dockets
State controller ledgers
Public licensing & entity APIs
workflow: Poll and normalize county/state record releases on an automated cadence
Cross-match entity/kinship/lien records and filter by minimum net fee threshold
Route verified dossiers into compliant outreach and claim execution
metrics: Cost per verified lead
Docket-to-contact latency (hours)
Net recovery / conversion rate

platform_risks.failure_mode: Portal rate-limiting or CAPTCHA gating
platform_risks.trigger: High-frequency automated polling against county or agency web portals
platform_risks.impact: Delayed lead ingestion or temporary IP block on target registry
platform_risks.detection_metric: HTTP 429/403 rate and daily record ingestion delta
platform_risks.fallback: Switch to scheduled bulk FOIA/public-record exports, official data feeds, and low-frequency cached queues

plays.name: DNS/Script Technographic Drop-Off & Renewal-Window Interception
plays.mechanism: Crawl target commercial domains and DNS TXT/CNAME records weekly to detect the exact day a company installs or removes high-ticket enterprise software tags (Salesforce, HubSpot, Marketo, Segment, NetSuite), predicting annual renewal windows (Month 10–11) and active vendor migrations.
inputs: Weekly HTTP script-tag, DOM header, & DNS TXT/CNAME technographic crawler
Historical install-timestamp ledger (calculating 12-month contract renewal windows)
B2B executive contact graph & migration-agency/SaaS partner routing
workflow: Scan 500,000+ target B2B domains weekly for JavaScript SDKs, tracking pixels, and SPF/CNAME records of $20k–$150k/yr SaaS platforms
Flag accounts entering Month 10 of their annual contract (60 days before auto-renewal lock-in) or accounts running dual competing tags during a live evaluation
Route renewal-window and active-churn signals to competing SaaS sales teams, software resellers, and implementation agencies
metrics: Install/drop detection precision (%) and renewal-date accuracy
Outbound reply-to-demo conversion rate on Month-10 renewal targets
Per-opportunity bounty or retainer revenue per agency/SaaS partner

platform_risks.failure_mode: WAF/Cloudflare bot-blocking or false-positive tag detection from server-side GTM
platform_risks.trigger: High-concurrency crawling from datacenter IPs or misinterpreting server-side tag manager consolidation as vendor churn
platform_risks.impact: Incomplete technographic diffs or wasted sales outreach on false churn signals
platform_risks.detection_metric: Crawler HTTP 200 success rate and multi-signal verification (DNS SPF/CNAME + careers-page job-posting confirmation)
platform_risks.fallback: Combine passive DNS TXT/CNAME monitoring with job-posting technographic mentions to confirm true vendor switches before routing

plays.name: Subsidized / Developer-Tenant Multi-Inbox Cold Outbound Infrastructure
plays.mechanism: Provisioning hundreds of isolated secondary domains across subsidized Microsoft 365 developer/partner tenants, Cloudflare Email Routing, and low-cost SMTP relays—sending strictly 15–25 plain-text emails per inbox per day across 300+ free/subsidized mailboxes to deliver 150,000+ monthly B2B cold emails into primary inboxes without paying $6–$12/seat retail Google Workspace pricing.
inputs: Lookalike secondary domain portfolio with automated SPF, DKIM (2048-bit), DMARC (`p=quarantine`/`reject`), and custom tracking-free MX records
Subsidized M365 partner/developer tenants, Cloudflare Email Routing catch-alls, and distributed SMTP sending nodes
Automated peer-to-peer warmup network and master unibox reply-routing webhook
workflow: Provision 100–300 secondary sending domains and bind 2–3 mailboxes per domain via automated DNS and tenant scripts
Warm every mailbox for 14–21 days with realistic thread-depth conversations before introducing live outbound prospects
Cap daily outbound volume at <=20 zero-link, zero-tracking-pixel plain-text messages per mailbox per day to stay completely beneath ESP volume heuristics
Aggregate all prospect replies into a single unified AI-triaged inbox that books qualified B2B sales calls on pay-per-show or retainer terms
metrics: Primary-inbox placement rate (%) across Gmail and Microsoft 365 seed tests
All-in monthly infrastructure cost per 10,000 delivered plain-text emails ($)
Positive reply rate (%) and booked meetings per 1,000 prospects contacted

platform_risks.failure_mode: Tenant-wide outbound throttling or domain-footprint blacklisting (Spamhaus DBL)
platform_risks.trigger: Placing too many domains inside a single tenant, embedding tracking pixels, or exceeding 30 sends/day per mailbox
platform_risks.impact: Tenant suspension or domain-level spam-folder routing
platform_risks.detection_metric: Daily seed-list inbox placement (%) and bounce rate (<1.5% hard threshold)
platform_risks.fallback: Enforce max 2–3 domains per tenant, strip all open/click tracking pixels, verify 100% of leads via SMTP catch-all checks before sending, and keep hot-standby warmed domains ready for instant swap

plays.name: High-Velocity DM Outbound & Trigger Funnels
plays.mechanism: Replace blind cold mass-DM blasts (which die to PeerFloodError and silent Message Request graveyards) with high-velocity comment-to-DM triggers, hand-raiser reaction hooks, and multi-inbox warm signal routing.
inputs: Short-form / community trigger posts ('Comment KEYWORD')
Signal-verified prospect handles
Automated DM qualification & booking bridge
workflow: Publish high-curiosity teardown or resource posts where prospects comment a trigger keyword or react to unlock a playbook or calculator
Deliver instant automated DM replies to warm hand-raisers (bypassing cold-DM filters because the user initiated interaction) or send contextual 1-to-1 DMs referencing an active public request
Qualify budget and timeline inside a 3-message DM micro-funnel and transition immediately to a booked call, checkout link, or owned SMS/email list
metrics: Trigger-comment to DM delivery rate
DM reply-to-qualified-conversation %
Revenue per 100 DM threads

platform_risks.failure_mode: PeerFloodError, shadow-filtering into 'Hidden Requests', or link-domain blacklisting
platform_risks.trigger: Sending identical unsolicited cold DMs with raw external URLs across freshly registered or SIM-farmed accounts
platform_risks.impact: Near-0% inbox placement, outbound DM block, or permanent account suspension
platform_risks.detection_metric: Seen/reply ratio below 10% and outbound PeerFloodError / action-block frequency
platform_risks.fallback: Require user-initiated trigger action (comment/reaction/inbound message) before automated DM dispatch and send external links only after the prospect replies

plays.name: Private B2B Group Purchasing Organization (GPO) Umbrella & Contingent Spend-Audit Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Pool 10,000–75,000+ seats and indirect corporate spend across hundreds of SMB member companies under authorized master GPO volume brackets through Una, OMNIA or private vertical SaaS, parcel and telecom GPOs. Pair negotiated brackets with quarter-end vendor price-floor benchmarking informed by Vendr/Tropic playbooks, targeting 3%–12% vendor-paid administrative rebates and 25%–35% contingent Year-1 shared-savings splits under no savings, no fee agreements. Eligibility, rebate bases and benchmark access must be verified; disclose dual compensation and avoid double-counting rebates in client savings.
inputs: Executed GPO member and supplier agreements defining eligible aggregated spend, volume brackets, administrative rebates and compensation disclosures
Member-authorized invoices and seat inventories plus lawfully obtained, like-for-like Vendr/Tropic-style pricing benchmarks
Contingent audit contracts defining the Year-1 savings baseline, exclusions, 25%–35% fee schedule and independent reconciliation rights
workflow: 1. Enroll eligible SMB members with written authority and aggregate verified seat demand and indirect spend without exchanging competitively sensitive data.
2. Validate GPO purchasing eligibility and negotiate supplier volume brackets using lawful quarter-end benchmarks for comparable service and commitment terms.
3. Present disclosed vendor rebates and contingent fees, secure member approval and implement authorized contract changes against an agreed savings baseline.
4. Reconcile actual Year-1 savings and vendor rebates, charge only earned shared-savings fees and audit bracket eligibility and renewal pricing.
metrics: Verified eligible seats and annual member spend within contracted GPO brackets
Realized Year-1 member savings net of contingent fees on a normalized baseline
Collected administrative rebates and shared-savings fees net of reversals

platform_risks.detection_metric: Unsupported eligible spend and disputed savings or rebates as a percentage of billed compensation
platform_risks.fallback: Suspend disputed fees, reconcile documented baselines with members and suppliers, refund unearned amounts and move affected members to eligible purchasing agreements
